display_name: National Insurance Law ss 334 and 337 and Schedule J, with the s 1 definitions they use: the reduced collection threshold, the rates of insurance contributions per branch and per column of insured person, and the arithmetic that applies them

run.method: one agent, one session, no sub-agents, from BRIEF.md

language.note: Identifiers and comments are English (@lang en). Hebrew is quoted only in `-- src:N |` comments generated mechanically from line N of the deposited source by tools/srcquote.py, and in short runs that tools/hebcheck.py checks occur verbatim in it. Schedule J's figures are generated from the source by tools/schedule_j.py.

published_figures.note: Figures the Law computes but does not print, taken from the National Insurance Institute's pages fetched 2026-10-06; URLs and sha256 in nii-il04-published-figures.l4 and NOTES.md section 7.

scope: Encoded: s 334(a) (its three definitions, the reduced collection threshold and both update paragraphs) and (b); s 337(a)(1), (a)(2) (for monthly advance periods), (b) (as the test whether an order is within the power) and (c); Schedule J in full, both tables, all items, figure columns and totals, with the editors' 2024-2027 notes; s 1 'employee', 'employer', 'self-employed person', 'the average wage' (with 'compensation', 'the compensation rate', 'update day'), 'the index', 'tax year', 'the Minister'. Every other s 1 term is listed out of scope. Inputs, not encoded: s 335 (which branches a person pays), ss 344-351 with s 348 and Schedule K (the income), s 342 (the deduction, row IL-05), s 336, s 340, s 2, s 28, s 32, Schedule A. Declined by name where they reach a case: s 341 (reduced rates by order), s 343 (reduced work-injury contributions), work injury of one who is neither (s 340(a)(2)), a '–' in the person's column, contribution months before 2026, an extension order under Amendment 252 s 7(b) for 2029 on, and the threshold for 2027 on unless supplied. (Before the repair of 2026-10-07 the temporary column D 'gap' was also declined; the enacted Laws remove it.) See NOTES.md sections 1-3.

years_answered.contribution months: January 2026 on; earlier months declined (the deposited s 334 and Schedule J are in force from 1 January 2026, verified against the 2025 budget-year Law s 21)
years_answered.reduced collection threshold: 2026 from the Institute's published figure; 2027 on only when the caller supplies it (index-updated 2027-2028, wage-updated from 2029)
years_answered.Schedule J version: 2026 temporary lower sub-columns with the 2024-2027 item-4 figure; 2027 permanent table with the 2024-2027 item-4 figures, or with an order under Amendment 252 s 7(b) the temporary lower sub-columns; 2028 permanent as printed, or with an order the temporary lower sub-columns; 2029 on permanent as printed. The year-only rules assume no order (A8).

expected_red.why: Schedule J's printed totals differ from the sums of its items in 10 cells across the four readings; the Institute's 2026 composites above the threshold exceed the items in 4 cases; and the 2025 text as enacted (item 2 at 0.17) did not meet its own printed total (1, added 2026-10-07). Findings about the source: NOTES.md section 0 and 'Repair 2026-10-07', fork F4. From 0.3.0 the two composite assertions that used the generic rule ask the items' reading by name, so they still compare the items with the Institute; at the default reading the employee's composites are reached (nii-il04-tests.l4).

The independent tester's module: five expectations of the pre-repair F3 (lines 756, 924, 929-931) that the enacted Laws overturned on 2026-10-07. At 0.3.0 a further 13 failed and 9 were refused against the new printed-totals default; at 0.3.1 the lead re-pointed those 22 (lines 505, 507-510, 801-803, 805-810, 846-848, 854, 856, 858, 895, 933) to fork F4's items' reading by name, values and inputs unchanged, because the tester decided that reading before the ruling. At 0.4.0 T7 (fork F6, line 787), which failed from 0.2.0 to 0.3.1, passes: a fall in the index is declined by default. Listed in check.sh (expected_failed 5). NOTES.md 'Version 0.3.1' and 'Version 0.4.0'. At 0.4.1 (BACKLOG IL-21) the five are classed TESTER-WRONG, inventory 04-TF3, and annotated by the lead in a second dated note at the end of the file (the 2025 Budget-year Law s 19(6) and s 21; the IL-07 independent tester's separate confirmation of the 7,703 boundary), values and inputs unchanged; they keep failing as the record of what the consolidation says. NOTES.md 'Version 0.4.1'.

forks.F1: Schedule J's years are the calendar years of the months for which contributions are paid. Confirmed 2026-10-07 by Amendment 252 s 7(a) ('in respect of the years 2025 and 2026').
forks.F2: Each table's 2024-2027 notes apply while that table is in force (the readings coincide in effect).
forks.F3: Revised 2026-10-07: from 1 January 2026 column D's upper part begins at the reduced collection threshold (2025 budget-year Law s 19(6) and s 21; Amendment 252 s 7(a)(3) replaced only the lower sub-columns); the consolidation's heading at line 4718 is stale. Before: the part between the threshold and 60% of the average wage was declined.
forks.F4: RULED by Meng on 2026-10-07 (backlog row IL-11, v0.3.0): where Schedule J's printed totals differ from the sums of its items (column D's upper part 7.00 against 4.67 in every version; column C above the threshold for an employee 14.60 against 14.49; in the permanent version column C not above the threshold for an employee 3.95 against 4.26), the printed totals govern by default, and the items' reading is kept as the alternative, by name. One switch: `Schedule J — the reading this row takes where its totals row and its items differ` in nii-schedule-j.l4. Fewer branches than the totals row covers, in a cell where the items do not reach the total, are declined at the printed totals. (0.1.0-0.2.0: the items were used for computing, the totals kept as data, compared red; evidence added 2026-10-07: s 20(1) of the 2025 budget-year Law and s 24 of the Economic Efficiency Law 5783-2023 each moved a row and its total together.)
forks.F5: Which average wage (s 1, 13,566, or s 2, 13,769 for 2026) the slice means is not decided; every rule takes it as an argument. After the F3 repair Schedule J no longer reads it; row IL-05 found the Institute's Chapter 15 figures fit the s 2 figure. (0.4.1, inventory 04-N14: the four column D rules in nii-schedule-j.l4 that still take the average wage say on the argument, in a @desc, that it is not read for 2026 on and that only the 2025 text kept as data reads it.)
forks.F6: RULED by Meng on 2026-10-07 (TRIDENT; backlog row IL-12, v0.4.0): s 334(a)(1)-(2) update the threshold by the rate of RISE of the index or the average wage and say nothing of a fall, so where the later reading is below the earlier the case is declined by default, this row's rule being to decline where the text does not decide. Three readings kept by name (`A reading of section 334(a) where the index or the average wage falls`): `the fall is applied` (this row's reading in 0.1.0-0.3.1), `the threshold stays where it was` (Axiom's, as BACKLOG row IL-12 records it), `a fall is declined` (the independent tester's T7, and the default). One switch: `section 334(a) — the reading this row takes where the index or the average wage falls` in nii-s334-interpretation.l4. A rise or no change is answered the same under all three. Meng declined on 2026-10-07 to look up the Institute's past practice as evidence: "whatever they did last time is no guarantee of how they'll do next time"; the default is not waiting on evidence. (0.1.0-0.3.1: a fall in the index or the average wage lowers the threshold (the formula as written).)
forks.F7: Nothing is rounded; the 2026 threshold is used as published.
forks.F8: s 337(a)(2): equal shares over the advance periods; monthly periods only, others declined.
forks.F9: s 337(c): the deduction is multiplied by the ratio of the new rate to the old.
forks.F10: A '–' is no figure, not a zero: a branch paid with a dash in the person's column is declined.
forks.F11: Whether the relative of a family-member employee is an 'employer' is not decided (no rule here turns on it).
forks.F12: A tax year is a calendar year; special assessment periods are not modelled.
forks.F13: The core of 'employee' is a person employed within an employment relationship (an input).
forks.F14: s 334(b)'s 'the payer is the employer' is recorded as a comment only.
forks.F15: Schedule J items 1 and 2 are one maternity branch; the column decides which item applies.
forks.F16: 'at least' and 'not less than' in 'self-employed person' are inclusive.
forks.F17: Column C is marginal: each figure on its part of the income.
forks.F18: The temporary lower sub-columns' own headings in Amendment 252 still say '60% of the average wage'; read as the reduced collection threshold (s 19(6) reaching Schedule J as read under the temporary provision), as the consolidation and the Institute do.
forks.F19: Item 4, employee, not above the split, 2026: Amendment 252's replaced sub-column (0.60) governs, not the Economic Efficiency Law's 0.47.
forks.F20: An extension order under Amendment 252 s 7(b) is an input per year; whether a 2028 order presupposes a 2027 one is not checked.
